routes.description: The highway, heat, crosswind and lava.
Kailua Bay, the swim start, Pacific water and race-morning calm.
Transition racks, timing, race history and the pier where the day begins.
The run home, Aliʻi Drive, the finish and the long light into night.
Athletes, winning machines and the decisions behind championship performances.
The long argument with air, position and the clock.
Speedmax heritage, engineering lineage and source-backed machine studies.
Airflow, position, drag and the mechanics of getting smaller.
Shoes, helmets, suits and the equipment that surrounds the athlete.
T1, T2, gear choices and the small rituals that save time when it matters.
Schedule, island changes and the useful chaos before race day.
Place, geology, wind, coffee and respectful context beyond the course.
Results, references, old machines and the sources behind the world.
Oddities, hidden objects, jokes and things that are better discovered than announced.
